purpose: Held-out ambiguity-boundary reference outcome for substantial simultaneous degradation of several business-critical services where the performance symptom is established but no common technical cause, definitive primary affected component or clear technical owner has been identified.

incident_summary_requirements: State that the Public API Gateway, Identity and Access Service and Order Management Service are simultaneously degraded.
State that all three services remain materially available and successful transactions continue.
Mention the elevated latency and non-total failure rates for API, authentication and order requests.
State that customers across the United Kingdom and Ireland are affected.
State that the available traces do not identify one shared component or consistent failing operation.
State that no direct application, infrastructure, network, dependency or configuration failure has been established.
Treat SVC-API only as a provisional primary area because it is the common entry point and has the highest observed timeout rate.
Do not claim that SVC-API caused the authentication or order degradation.
Do not route definitively to one technical application or platform team.

severity.rationale: Several Tier 1 customer services are substantially degraded across a widespread population, failure and latency levels are significant and no reliable workaround exists. Successful transactions continue and no service is completely unavailable, supporting High rather than Critical severity.

incident_category.rationale: The directly supported condition across all three services is material degradation in latency and reliability while core functionality remains available. No evidence supports a more specific application, infrastructure, network, dependency or configuration category.

affected_area.rationale: SVC-API is the common request entry point and has the highest directly observed timeout rate, making it the most defensible provisional primary area. SVC-AUTH and SVC-ORDER are directly degraded additional areas, but the evidence does not establish that SVC-API caused their symptoms or that any one component is the common technical source.

routing.rationale: Ownership is unclear because the evidence spans services owned by RG-NETWORK, RG-IAM and RG-COMMERCE without directly implicating one technical component. The ownership policy therefore requires provisional routing to RG-OPS for initial coordination until a technical owner is established.

prohibited_recommendations: declare the Public API Gateway to be the common root cause
route definitively to RG-NETWORK, RG-IAM or RG-COMMERCE
restart, redeploy or scale multiple services
change API routing, DNS, firewall or load-balancer configuration
change authentication, order-processing or database configuration
roll back a deployment without direct evidence
initiate broad remediation across multiple systems
automatically retry or replay failed order transactions
claim that one common technical cause has been definitively established
claim that any investigative, coordination or remedial action has already been completed

information_gaps: Whether the three service degradations share one common cause or represent multiple concurrent conditions.
The independently verified latency contribution and health of each relevant application and platform dependency.
The definitive primary affected component and technical resolver group.
The expected duration and recovery time for normal multi-service performance.
Whether failed order submissions created partial records or duplicate-processing risk.

assessment_notes: The performance category is non-provisional because substantial latency and non-total failure rates are directly measured across all affected services.
The primary affected area is provisional because no common technical source has been established.
SVC-API is selected only as the most defensible provisional focal point; it must not be represented as the confirmed cause of downstream degradation.
RG-OPS is the correct provisional primary resolver under the unclear-ownership routing policy. No separate coordination group is required because RG-OPS is itself the coordinating primary group.
RB-012 is specifically intended for multi-service incidents where common cause and ownership remain unclear.
The scenario is materially distinct from DEV-003 and EVAL-007 because it contains no directly evidenced shared-platform failure and no complete service outage.
